title: Free coherent cone modules: collage structure and point formula
statement:
Use small simplicial categories and the colimit construction $\mathfrak C$ of [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching]. Fix a small simplicial category $A$, a small simplicial set $S$, and a simplicial functor $a:\mathfrak C[S]\to A$. For $p:X\to S$, define the ordered join $X\star\Delta^0$ by adjoining a last vertex $v$: its degree-$r$ simplices are $X_r$, the constant cone simplex, and one copy of $X_j$ for each $0\leq j<r$, interpreted as an initial $X$-segment followed by vertices at $v$. Let
$$M_p=A\amalg_{\mathfrak C[X]}\mathfrak C[X\star\Delta^0],\qquad L_a(X)(c)=M_p(c,v).$$
The action is precomposition, so $L_a(X)$ is a simplicial functor $A^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{sSet}$. Then the full subcategory of $M_p$ on the objects of $A$ is exactly $A$, the mapping sets $M_p(v,c)$ are empty, and $M_p(v,v)=\Delta^0$. For a simplicial set $K$ over a vertex $s$, there is a natural isomorphism
$$L_a(K\to\{s\}\to S)(c)\cong A(c,a(s))\times |K|_Q,$$
where $|K|_Q=\int^{[n]}K_n\times Q^n$ and $Q^n$ is the pinched cosimplicial object of [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching]; the coend is the quotient identifying $(K(\alpha)z,q)$ with $(z,Q(\alpha)q)$. At $K=\Delta^0$ this is the representable $A(-,a(s))$. All displayed identifications commute with maps of $K$, $S$ and $A$. All constructions use small sets in the chosen universe.

source.place: Section 2.2.1, correspondence construction (the cone collage $M_p$); Section 2.2.2, point calculation (straightening over a vertex is the $Q$-realization). Read online on 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this simplicial homotopy result.

proof.text: The category of small simplicial categories has the small colimits used here by [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting]. The construction of [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching] preserves simplicial-set colimits, as follows directly from its defining universal property. For a simplicial category $E$, let $N_E$ have $n$-simplices the simplicial functors $\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]\to E$, with operators given by precomposition. A functor $\mathfrak C[T]\to E$ is, by the defining simplex colimit, a compatible such functor for every simplex of $T$, hence exactly a simplicial map $T\to N_E$. A map from a colimit of simplicial sets to $N_E$ is a compatible family of maps. The same is therefore true of functors from its $\mathfrak C$-image to $E$, proving the colimit claim. In particular this applies to every pinch pushout used below. No preservation assertion about individual mapping spaces of arbitrary simplicial-category colimits is made.

source.place: §2.2.1, correspondence definition; Example 2.2.2.5; expanded mapping-out argument

proof.text: Compute the cone category $B=\mathfrak C[X\star\Delta^0]$ from its presentation as a simplex colimit. Concretely, in each simplicial degree a colimit of enriched categories is formed by words of arrows from the input categories, identifying objects along the diagram and quotienting by the input identities, compositions and diagram maps. This is a direct construction: concatenation gives composition, simplex operators act on every letter, the relations are stable under those operators, and maps out are precisely compatible enriched functors out of the inputs. Every simplex of the cone is either an old $X$-simplex, the constant simplex at $v$, or a mixed simplex. A mixed simplex with an initial $X$-segment of dimension $j$ is a degeneracy, repeating only $v$, of the cone on that $j$-simplex. The subset-poset formula of [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching] says that its restriction to the initial face is exactly the corresponding $\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]$, that there are no arrows from its last vertex to an earlier vertex, and that the last-vertex endomorphism space is a point. Thus a word ending at an old object cannot pass through $v$. All relations with old endpoints are exactly the simplex-colimit relations for $X$: restriction of a cone-simplex operator with old endpoints is the operator of its initial face. A word starting at $v$ is an identity word. It follows that $B$ has the full old subcategory $\mathfrak C[X]$, no arrows from $v$ to old objects, and only the identity of $v$ as endomorphism. This includes $X=\varnothing$, where $B$ is the one-object identity category.

source.place: §2.2.1, cone correspondence; direct degreewise word presentation

proof.text: Apply the same word construction to $A\amalg_{\mathfrak C[X]}B$. Its object set can be chosen to be $\operatorname{Ob}(A)\amalg\{v\}$: each old vertex of $B$ is identified with its prescribed image in $A$, and $v$ is not identified with an old vertex. A word between objects of $A$ cannot pass through $v$, and all its $B$-letters are old letters, so the amalgamation relations replace them by their images in $A$. Conversely every relation on such words is an identity, a composition, or a diagram relation already valid in $A$. Therefore the old mapping simplicial sets and compositions are exactly those of $A$. The same no-return argument gives empty $M_p(v,c)$ and $M_p(v,v)=\Delta^0$. Composition induces the action $M_p(c,v)\times A(c',c)\to M_p(c',v)$. Associativity and identities in $M_p$ are the enriched functor axioms for $L_a$. This argument allows $a\mathfrak C[p]$ to identify vertices or arrows; it does not assume it is an inclusion.

source.place: §2.2.1, the amalgamated correspondence; explicit no-return word computation

proof.text: First compute the constant simplex $K=\Delta^n$ over $s$. Write $b=a(s)$. Its base functor factors through the one-object identity category $\{x\}$, so every old mapping simplex is sent to the identity simplex of $b$. By Step 1, collapsing this base face in $\mathfrak C[\Delta^{n+1}]$ gives $\mathfrak C[J^n]$, where $J^n=(\Delta^n\star\{v\})\amalg_{\Delta^n}\{x\}$. By [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching] its forward mapping set is $Q^n$; Step 3, applied with base category $\{x\}$ to the cone on $\Delta^n$, gives identity endomorphisms at $x$ and $v$ and the empty reverse mapping set. Thus this application is to the pinched pushout, not to a claim that $J^n$ itself is an ordered cone. Attach this two-object category to $A$ at $x=b$. Every new word from $c$ to $v$ is now an $A$-arrow from $c$ to $b$ followed by exactly one $Q^n$-arrow. Consecutive $A$-arrows compose, and the only further relations are their associative and identity relations. Hence the map $(f,q)\mapsto q\circ f$ is a bijection in every simplicial degree from $A(c,b)\times Q^n$ to the new mapping set. Its inverse reads the composed old prefix and the last forward letter; it is unaffected by any relation. Simplex operators act on both factors, so these bijections are a simplicial isomorphism. For a monotone map $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, its map is $(f,q)\mapsto(f,Q(\alpha)q)$, because the base remains the same constant vertex.

source.place: §2.2.2, definition of J and Q, printed p. 76; expanded attachment to an arbitrary A

proof.text:
For general $K\to\{s\}$, retain one common copy of $A$ and one common vertex $v$, even if $K$ is empty. A functor out of its amalgamated cone is a functor on $A$, the image of $v$, and compatible extensions on $\mathfrak C[\Delta^n\star\{v\}]$ for all simplices $z\in K_n$, whose old faces are the fixed constant-base functor. Indeed every mixed cone simplex has an initial $K$-simplex followed by repeated $v$; restriction and degeneracy of these simplices impose precisely this compatibility, while constant cone simplices only specify the already chosen $v$. Applying Step 4 to these pieces, their new mapping simplices are represented by triples $(f,z,q)$ with $f\in A(c,b)_r$, $z\in K_n$ and $q\in(Q^n)_r$. The compatibility relations are exactly
$$(f,K(\alpha)z,q)\sim(f,z,Q(\alpha)q),\qquad \alpha:[m]\to[n],\ z\in K_n,\ q\in(Q^m)_r.$$
There are no additional mixed compositions, since no arrow leaves $v$ for $A$. This quotient, with old category $A$, precomposition on $f$, and identity at $v$, has the preceding mapping-out property: a functor on $A$ and the image $w$ of $v$ being fixed, an action-compatible map from a simplex piece is determined by its value $t(q)$ on $(\mathrm{id}_b,q)$; its value on $(f,q)$ must be $t(q)\circ F(f)$. Conversely this formula defines an action-compatible map for every simplicial map $t:Q^n\to E(F(b),w)$. The coend relations say precisely that these maps agree under every simplex operator. Hence maps out are exactly the compatible functors on the simplex pieces, with their common $A$-action. It therefore computes the desired amalgamated cone. This proves the quotient formula directly, rather than assuming that taking a mapping set commutes with arbitrary enriched colimits.

source.place: §2.2.2, Remark 2.2.2.1 and the point construction; direct compatible-family quotient

proof.text:
Every generating relation of Step 5 fixes $f$. Consequently its equivalence classes are exactly pairs $(f,[z,q])$: surjectivity chooses any representative of $[z,q]$, and injectivity follows because a chain of generating relations preserves $f$ and is precisely a chain defining the second-factor coend. The resulting degreewise inverse maps are $[f,z,q]\mapsto(f,[z,q])$ and $(f,[z,q])\mapsto[f,z,q]$. Both commute with simplex operators. Thus
$$L_a(K\to\{s\}\to S)(c)\cong A(c,b)\times\int^{[n]}K_n\times Q^n.$$
Precomposition sends $(f,[z,q])$ to $(f\circ h,[z,q])$, so this is also an isomorphism of enriched presheaves, not just of their values. For $K=\varnothing$ the new mapping sets are empty, as is the coend, while $A$ and $v$ still exist.

source.place: §2.2.2, Remark 2.2.2.1; explicit inverse maps on the coend quotient

proof.text: For $K=\Delta^0$, all its simplices are the degeneracies of its unique vertex. The coend relation for the unique $[n]\to[0]$ sends every $[z,q]$ to its image in $Q^0=\Delta^0$ by [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching]. This identifies the coend with $\Delta^0$ and Step 6 becomes $A(-,a(s))$. For $u:K\to K'$ the formula is $(f,[z,q])\mapsto(f,[u(z),q])$. For a simplicial map $h:S\to S'$ and an enriched functor $F:A\to A'$ satisfying $Fa=a'\mathfrak C[h]$, the pushout-induced map sends $[f,z,q]$ to $[F(f),z,q]$, over the vertex $h(s)$; it preserves the defining relations and composition. These formulas agree before and after the displayed isomorphism, proving the claimed naturality in all parameters. Finally the simplex indices, generators, finite words and relations are small sets: they are indexed by the small sets of simplices and objects, countably many degrees and finite lengths. Their products, disjoint unions and quotients therefore stay in the chosen universe. No Kan, cofibrancy, quasicategory or model-structure hypothesis is used.
